assumptions: The requested metric was interpreted as average latency of failed attempts, computed by custom SQL because the catalog only exposes p95 latency (assumed p95_latency_ms as the governed metric).
The time window assumed was 2024-10-31 to 2026-10-31, but available data starts 2026-08-01.
Period analysed for data-quality checks: 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-31.
caveats: The data covers only 1 August 2026 onwards, so the two-year window requested could not be answered in full; the custom query was also capped at a shorter window than two years because the validator rejected the full span.

Part of this answer uses custom SQL written by the AI, outside the governed semantic layer. It was validated (read-only, governed views only, role filters applied) before running, but its logic has not been reviewed like the governed metrics.
Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once, keeping the first ingestion.

Missing issuer IDs: 8.0% of Meridian Bank's card attempts in 2026-08 (2,856 of 35,507) have no issuer_id; expected 0%. Issuer-level results for this scope are understated. Rows are kept and shown as '(missing)' issuer.
Attempt volume spiked +39% versus the usual level for 18 Oct to 31 Oct (14 days). Real sales events and data gaps both look like this; check before comparing totals across this period.

facts.text: Average authorization latency of failed attempts was 2,558.80 ms for issuer declines (37,617 failed attempts).
Average authorization latency of failed attempts was 3,204.29 ms for risk declines (12,544 failed attempts).
Average authorization latency of failed attempts was 12,017.64 ms for customer drop-offs (45,910 failed attempts).
Average authorization latency of failed attempts was 17,422.49 ms for technical failures (23,887 failed attempts).

response.headline: The data only supports a partial answer: failed payments have no single average latency, and it varies widely by failure type, from about 2,559 ms for issuer declines to 17,422 ms for technical failures.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Look at the latency distribution (median and percentiles) for these categories and check how many attempts sit at timeout thresholds.
hypotheses.rationale: Technical failures and customer drop-offs show far higher averages than issuer or risk declines, which are decisive responses that return quickly.
hypotheses.text: The long latencies for technical failures and customer drop-offs may reflect timeouts or abandoned sessions rather than genuine authorization processing time.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Average authorization latency of failed attempts was 17,422.49 ms for technical failures (23,887 failed attempts).
recommendations.rationale: The categories differ by several times, so a single average would be dominated by technical failures and customer drop-offs.
recommendations.text: Report latency by failure category (or use median/percentiles) instead of one blended average for failed payments.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The long latencies for technical failures and customer drop-offs may reflect timeouts or abandoned sessions rather than genuine authorization processing time.
recommendations.rationale: They have the highest average latency of any failure type.
recommendations.text: Investigate technical failures first, checking for timeouts at specific acquirers or payment methods.
